title: Index to Monographs #01-#15
note: Monograph #16 (Zybach & Islam 2000) was compiled but never digitised. This is a rebuild of the series index from the fifteen printed back-of-book indexes, as a living merged index.
method_notes: Source: the printed back-of-book indexes of monographs #01-#15 as captured in each record's index_entries[] (5,790 printed index lines). No index line was invented; nothing was added from the transcripts.

MERGING: headings are matched on a normalised key (case-folded, diacritics stripped, '&'='and', punctuation and bracketed qualifiers dropped) plus singularisation of an explicit list of unmistakable plural rubric words (Roads/Road, Creeks/Creek, Schools/School, Towns/Town ...). Word-order and spelling variants of Bob's own umbrella rubrics are merged through a hand-checked alias table (e.g. 'Oregon Towns and Cities' = 'Oregon Cities & Towns'; 'Cities & Towns' = 'Oregon Cities & Towns'). Personal names are never singularised.

DISPLAY: the displayed heading is always one of Bob's own printed forms - the literal that appears in the most monographs (ties resolved to the mixed-case form, then the longest). Every other printed form is kept in variants[].

NAME FOLDING: monograph #01 alone prints personal names on two tiers (heading = SURNAME, subheading = GIVEN NAME). Those 43 lines, and lines in other monographs whose joined form matches a comma-form heading printed in a different monograph, are folded to Bob's own majority form 'Surname, Given'. The two-tier originals are recorded in variants[].

PAGE ANCHORS: every reference is kept as {zc_id, mono, page} and rendered in Bob's monograph:page style ('05:47'). Printed ranges ('33-35') are expanded to their member pages, each carrying the printed form. Roman front-matter folios are kept as roman strings, never coerced to integers.

DRIFT (#06, #07): the printed index folios of #06 and #07 were compiled against an earlier pagination and run AHEAD of the text (#06 +0..+2, #07 +2..+7). The printed folio is always retained in `page`. Verification is two-pass: (1) for each reference, search the record's transcript text of pages p, p-1 ... p-dmax for the entry's own term, collecting every drift value that matches; (2) fit a drift curve d(page) from the references that matched at exactly one offset (median over a +/-6-page window), then resolve ambiguous references to the candidate offset nearest the curve. Offset 0 -> `page_verified`; offset d>0 -> `page_corrected` = p-d, with `method` naming the probe term and the offset.
SPOT-CHECK: 30 references drawn at random (seed 20000216) from the other thirteen monographs were tested the same way against their own transcripts.

CLASSIFICATION: kind is decided in this order - (1) Bob's own umbrella rubric (including the Tampico-concordance rubrics Camps, Creeks, Fires, Floods, Forts, Newspapers, Peaks and Hills, Post Offices, Roads and Trails, Schools, Towns and Cities, recorded in concordance_category); (2) the narrator/contributor roster; (3) the printed 'Surname, Given' name form; (4) the monograph records' own category fields (majority vote); (5) the records' places_mentioned gazetteer and its kind; (6) organisation / landform / event words in the name. kind_method records which rule fired.

CROSS-REFERENCES: 'See X' on a page-less entry becomes see[]; 'See also X', 'Also called X' and see-alsos embedded in a printed heading ('Trees [See also: Fruit & Nuts]') become see_also[]. Each is resolved to an entry_id where a matching entry exists; unresolved targets keep their text with resolved=false.

NOT DONE: page references that fall outside a record's transcript coverage (appendices, scan gaps - printed p.107 of #10, pp.76-77 of #12) cannot be machine-verified and carry page_verified=null, page_corrected=null.
